sources.citation: Taber, Mark. 1993. Toward a better understanding of the indigenous languages of Southwestern Maluku. Oceanic Linguistics 32(2): 389-441 -- as keyed in LexiRumah 3.0.0 (Kaiping, Edwards & Klamer eds. 2019; lect nila1244, source taber93, 190 forms, Kokroman village) and in ABVD language 305 (120 forms)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Data only (Taber's stress marks): LexiRumah keying 170/190 penult (ˈleʋra 'sun', ˈhulna 'moon', ˈknɔrna 'star', ˈlakti 'sky', ˈhatu 'stone'), 8 final (demonstratives ijanˈɛ 'this', ijaˈjɛ 'that'; prefixed verbs nɔ+mˈni 'drink', nauˈti 'give'), 7 monosyllables, 4 double-marked compounds, 1 antepenult (itˈwakila 'all'); ABVD keying 107/120 penult. The article's own prose (transcription preface) was not accessible.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record nila1244; Wikipedia 'Nila language'; Endangered Languages Project lang/2726; Garuda search 'bahasa Nila' (0 documents)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliographic only: Glottolog meds = van Engelenhoven 2003 (phonology or text collection, 6 pp.) and Stokhof 1981 (wordlist); Wikipedia stub cites Taber 1993 only; ELP page is a JS shell; no Indonesian-journal literature on Nila indexed in Garuda.

sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. & Owen Edwards. 2026. The Austronesian languages of eastern Indonesia and Timor-Leste: Unravelling their prehistory and classification. Berlin: Language Science Press (526)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 4.6.4 Teun-Nila-Serua (pp. 217-223): historical phonology with Nila (Wotay, Edwards 2023a) and Nila (Kokroman, Taber 1993) data cited without stress marks; no Nila stress statement. Only a generic remark p. 115 (Flores schwa discussion): 'While penultimate stress is the normal rule for Wallacean languages, words with penultimate schwa can have stress on other syllables.'

sources.citation: Edwards, Owen. 2025. Teun, Nila, Serua (Indonesia) - A collection of language snapshots. Language Documentation and Description 25(1): 1-12. DOI 10.25894/ldd.2615
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sociolinguistic snapshot; pp. 6-7 note two Nila varieties (Rumdai *f > h vs Wotay/Sifluru f) and state 'To date, Taber is the only published data on Nila.' Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Edwards, Owen. 2023. Emplawas and languages of the Babar islands (ELAR deposit IPF0417): Nila text bundles (e.g. 'Childhood stories / Cerita waktu masih kecil', 'Asking for Ajung and Arah to build a house') and audio of NIL001/NIL005 wordlists.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Audio recordings of the Nila wordlist and texts would allow an instrumental/auditory check of stress placement; some text bundles are restricted (U_UserAccess). No sketch grammar found in the deposit.

sources.citation: Edwards, Owen. 2023. Nila wordlist 1 / Daftar kata bahasa Nila 1 (bundle NIL001, Wotay village, 8 Dec 2023), in 'Emplawas and languages of the Babar islands' (ELDP IPF0417), Endangered Languages Archive. hdl:2196/eed771a3-6949-4ad0-b694-6294a973f98f
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Typed 481-item list (+24 possessive phrases, sentences) has phonemic forms without stress marks and no transcription note. The 12-page handwritten field form (scan, no text layer; pages 1 and 6 viewed) carries stress marks on phonetic forms: ˈʔetna 'tree', ˈtofu, ˈfia 'banana', maˈmama 'betel', ˈlotna, ˈmatra 'eye', ˈnafu 'nose', ˈlima 'hand', ˈklina 'ear', niruˈmatra 'face', lɛˈlɛnʔa 'neck' -- overwhelmingly penultimate. Primary data only; no statement.

sources.citation: van Engelenhoven, Aone. 2003. Language endangerment in Indonesia: The incipient obsolescence and acute death of Teun, Nila and Serua (Central and Southwest Maluku). In Mark Janse & Sijmen Tol (eds.), Language Death and Language Maintenance (CILT 240), 49-80. Amsterdam: Benjamins. DOI 10.1075/cilt.240.05eng
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Sec. 3 'Typology' (pp. 52-55) gives a Serua phoneme inventory, plural -rV, metathesis and possession; Nila appears only in sociolinguistic passages and in Table 4 (p. 55) possessive forms taken from Taber 1993. The words 'stress'/'accent' occur only in non-linguistic senses. Nothing on stress for Nila (or Serua). This is Glottolog's Glottolog's most extensive description for Nila.

sources.citation: Collins, James T. 1982. Linguistic research in Maluku: A report of recent field work. Oceanic Linguistics 21(1/2): 73-146.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: Field report that discusses the TNS isolects (f/h isogloss, Collins 1982:124 per van Engelenhoven 2003); may contain brief phonological notes on Nila including stress.

sources.citation: Stokhof, W.A.L. (ed.). 1981. Holle lists: vocabularies in languages of Indonesia vol. 3/2, Central Moluccas: Seram (II) (PL D-44), list 224b 'Niala' (Boemei, 1937), pp. 161-174
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Glottolog lists it as a Nila wordlist, but Edwards 2025 fn. 5 and Grimes & Edwards 2026: 217 fn. 23 show it is Teun of Bumei village. Bare Dutch-spelling wordlist, no stress marks, nothing on stress.
